svg.text: Everyday English - Quote
Give your next step more
attention than your last
stumble.
MEANING
Focus on a useful action after a setback instead of
dwelling on the mistake.
IN CONTEXT
After a difficult presentation, her colleague said, “Give
your next step more attention than your last stumble.”
She decided to rehearse the opening again.
USAGE NOTE
Stumble is a metaphor for a minor mistake; next step
means the next action. Use the line to redirect
attention after acknowledging the problem, not to
dismiss its consequences.
CONVERSATION
A: I cannot stop thinking about my mistake.
B: “Give your next step more attention than your last
stumble.” What could you change?
A: I could check the figures before presenting.
B: Good. That addresses the problem directly.
YOUR TURN
Use the quote after acknowledging a setback, then
suggest a concrete action. Model: The error mattered.
Now check the figures and send a correction.
